title: Indus script: machine-readable seal catalogues from Mackay (1938) and Marshall (1931), with photo-coded text features and a reproducible analysis pipeline
description:
Two machine-readable catalogues of Mohenjo-daro seals, transcribed by hand from the excavation reports: Mackay (1938), 709 rows with block, house, room and level; Marshall (1931), 560 rows with excavation area and depth. With them: text features coded from all thirteen of Mackay's seal plates (531 seals, 419 joined to find-spots, coder reliability kappa 0.89), a held-out validated set of 90 distributional constraints on Indus sign sequences, and a reproducible pipeline of structural comparisons against Sumerian, Egyptian (Old/Middle and Later), Linear A/B, proto-cuneiform and Proto-Elamite corpora.

The analytical results are mainly negative and are documented as such: text form does not vary with depth or neighbourhood across the complete coded corpus, and one earlier positive result failed to replicate on independent data. Most script-internal findings replicate published work (Yadav et al. 2010; Mahadevan; Mukhopadhyay; Kriger & Hunt 2026); see docs/PRIOR_WORK.md. No decipherment is offered or implied.
notes: Code MIT; transcribed and coded data CC BY 4.0; third-party corpora under their own licences (see docs/DATA_NOTICE.md). Companion preprint (docs/RESEARCH_NOTE.md): https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22852774
